title: The State of Sovereign AI Adoption (Research) | Cohere
gist: A Cohere-commissioned IDC survey of 500+ senior decision-makers at $1B+ enterprises in Canada, the US, UK, and Germany finds sovereign AI is a stated priority for over half of executives yet one in three cannot define it, with data leakage and compliance the top concerns across regulated industries (Financial Services 82%). Cohere uses the findings to position its privately deployable North platform against centralized big-tech AI, arguing enterprises now want to control, not rent, their AI.

themes.theme: Drivers of the sovereign AI shift

insights.claim: Recent model access restrictions and high-profile cybersecurity incidents have exposed the fragility of AI delivered through centralized big-tech platforms, pushing enterprises and governments to re-architect AI strategies around avoiding single points of failure and vendor lock-in.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Watch for enterprise AI budget rotation away from centralized API-only providers toward deployable/private-model vendors and sovereign cloud offerings.
insights.quote: Recent model access restrictions and several high-profile cybersecurity incidents have become a global wake-up call, exposing how fragile technological dependencies can be.
insights.locator: Over the past year, enterprises and governments

insights.claim: Critical regulated industries — healthcare, financial services, energy, telecom, manufacturing — operating with sensitive data increasingly want to own and control their AI stacks rather than rent them from external providers.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Regulated verticals are the beachhead market for on-prem/air-gapped AI deployment; vendors with private-deployment architectures gain an edge there.
insights.quote: seeking to control, not rent, their AI
insights.locator: These events highlight a broader structural

insights.claim: As AI becomes the control layer for critical infrastructure — financial systems, energy grids, telecom networks, manufacturing supply chains — sovereign AI shifts from a compliance preference to an operational necessity.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Implies a durable, non-cyclical demand base for sovereign AI infrastructure tied to national-security and resilience mandates, not just AI hype cycles.
insights.quote: as AI becomes the control layer for critical infrastructure, from financial systems and energy grids to telecom networks and manufacturing supply chains, sovereign AI is an operational necessity

insights.claim: More than half of executive leaders say sovereign AI is a priority, yet there is little agreement on its definition and one in three leaders could not describe it in their own words.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: A priority without a shared definition means early, unconsolidated demand — vendors who define the category (as Cohere is attempting) can capture the framing and the RFPs.
insights.quote: while more than half of executive leaders believe sovereign AI is a priority, there is little agreement on the definition, and many cannot define it.

insights.claim: Only 13% of enterprise leaders are 'very widely' aware of sovereign AI, meaning AI purchasing decisions in large organizations are being made without sufficient context on sovereignty requirements.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Low awareness plus stated priority signals a large education-led sales cycle ahead; expect heavy analyst/marketing spend to shape the category before budgets consolidate.
insights.quote: Only 13% of leaders are “very widely” aware, revealing a fragmented and inconsistent grasp of the concept across global organizations.

insights.claim: Among leaders who can define sovereign AI, 52% frame it as local or national control and 35% invoke digital independence, anchoring the concept in geopolitics rather than pure technology terms.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Sovereignty demand is politically anchored — national data-localization policy and geopolitical tension are the demand catalysts to monitor, not model benchmarks.

insights.claim: Sovereign AI is interpreted differently by role: line-of-business leaders see it as business-risk management (data security, privacy, cost control) while IT leaders see it as regulatory compliance — and IT professionals show twice the awareness of LOB leaders.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Sovereign AI vendors must sell two different value propositions in the same account; IT is currently the more informed buyer champion.
insights.quote: Notably, IT professionals show two times higher awareness than LOB leaders.

themes.theme: Survey data: concerns and competitive advantage

insights.claim: Data leakage, privacy, compliance, and regulatory risk are the top concerns sovereign AI is expected to address in every industry surveyed, led by Financial Services (82%), Manufacturing (77%), Telco (75%), Healthcare (74%), and Energy (70%).
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Security/compliance, not capability, is the purchase trigger — favors vendors and clouds selling data residency, private deployment, and audit features over frontier-model performance.
insights.locator: Data leakage and compliance are top concerns

insights.claim: The largest enterprises (around $20B USD in revenue) are much more risk-aware about AI sovereignty than small firms, so sovereign AI demand concentrates at the top of the enterprise market.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Sovereign AI vendors' revenue will skew to mega-cap enterprise and government accounts — long sales cycles but large, sticky contracts.
insights.locator: Data leakage and compliance are top concerns

insights.claim: Competitive advantage is an emerging (not yet top) driver of sovereign AI adoption, strongest in Canada (35%) and the US (28%) versus Germany (23%) and the UK (18%), and by industry led by Telco (37%) and Manufacturing (32%).
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: North America frames sovereignty offensively (differentiation) while Europe frames it defensively (regulation) — expect different buying criteria and sales motions by region.
insights.locator: Competitive advantage is also an emerging trend

insights.claim: IDC predicts that by 2028 CIOs at multinational organizations will boost investments in modular, sovereign-ready cloud and data localization environments by 65% to future-proof against rising sovereignty demands.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: A quantified multi-year capex tailwind for sovereign/localized cloud infrastructure, regional data centers, and deployable AI software.
insights.quote: By 2028, CIOs at multinational organizations will boost investments in modular, sovereign-ready cloud and data localization environments by 65% to future-proof operations against rising sovereignty demands.

insights.claim: Sovereign AI adoption is blocked by three gaps: no clear blueprint for operationalizing sovereignty despite recognized vendor lock-in risk, fragmented awareness across organizations, and an awareness-to-action gap in building strategies with clear C-suite ownership — with the right owning role varying by country.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Adoption will lag stated intent until governance blueprints mature — services firms and consultancies that operationalize sovereignty stand to benefit first.
insights.locator: Three blockers slowing sovereign AI adoption

insights.claim: Enterprises in regulated industries and geopolitically sensitive markets are re-architecting digital operating models from a global-by-default posture to a deliberately sovereign-by-design approach.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Structural fragmentation of the global cloud/AI stack — a headwind for one-size-global hyperscaler models, a tailwind for regional and deployable AI infrastructure.
insights.quote: shifting from a global-by-default posture to a deliberately sovereign-by-design approach

insights.claim: Cohere positions its models and agentic AI platform North as running entirely within a customer's own infrastructure and jurisdiction — including on-premises and fully air-gapped deployments — with no risk of external shutdown or remote override, in direct contrast to centralized API-delivered AI.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Cohere is betting its differentiation on private deployment rather than frontier capability — a read on where a second-tier model lab sees defensible enterprise ground versus OpenAI/Anthropic/Google.
insights.quote: run entirely within a customer’s chosen infrastructure and jurisdiction, with no risk of external shutdown or remote override

insights.claim: The findings come from a Cohere-commissioned IDC InfoBrief surveying 500+ senior AI-purchasing decision-makers at enterprises with over $1B in annual revenue across Canada, the US, UK, and Germany, fielded April–May 2026 and skewed to regulated industries.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Vendor-sponsored research aligned with the sponsor's product thesis — treat the directional trend as real but discount the framing; sample excludes Asia and most of the EU.
